key_insight: A multimodal graph neural network can prioritize and distinguish approved, prospective, and novel cancer immunotherapy targets, and top candidates can be functionally validated using patient-derived tumour explants, linking prediction to clinically relevant validation.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of prioritizing actionable immunotherapy targets from complex, multimodal biomedical data and bridging computational predictions with experimental, patient-relevant validation.
method: Develop a multimodal graph neural network that integrates molecular, clinical, and interaction-network data to score candidate targets.
Train the model to distinguish approved and prospective targets and rank novel candidates for follow-up.
Validate high-ranked predictions using a clinically relevant patient-derived tumour explant platform to confirm functional relevance.
impact: Provides a reproducible pipeline combining GNN-based target prioritization with ex vivo validation, offering a template for ML practitioners aiming to produce clinically actionable predictions in drug discovery and translational research.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: data inputs → multimodal GNN → ranked target list → patient-derived explant validation
Graph schematic showing node/edge types and multimodal feature integration
Ranking visualization (e.g., bar or waterfall chart) highlighting approved, prospective, and novel candidates
Photo or icon-based depiction of the patient-derived tumour explant assay used for validation
paper_title: Immunotherapy drug target identification using machine learning and patient-derived tumour explant validation
paper_authors: Marcellus Augustine, Nuno Rocha Nene, Hongchang Fu, Christopher L. Pinder, Lorena Ligammari
